modelResponse.episodeSummary: 74yo female, Torsades de Pointes, critical severity, hemodynamically unstable (MAP 49)
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Sinusoidal amplitude modulation with axis twisting
preEventNote: Baseline ECG 6 min prior: sinus 62, marked QT prolongation QTc 618 ms, prominent U waves
modelResponse.primaryEtiology: Drug-induced Long QT Syndrome (diLQTS) exacerbated by electrolyte depletion
modelResponse.mechanism: Synergistic prolongation of the ventricular action potential (delayed repolarization) caused by Sotalol, Azithromycin, and Ondansetron, triggered by severe hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, leading to early afterdepolarizations (EADs) and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
contributingFactors: Recent gastroenteritis with vomiting/diarrhea x3 days

rejectedAlternatives.why: troponinT 0.02 ng/mL is only mildly high (rate-related) and no ST deviation noted on baseline; clinical context points strongly to repolarization delay.
ECG morphology specifically describes 'axis twisting' and 'sinusoidal amplitude modulation' characteristic of TdP.

recommendedActions: Immediate defibrillation/unsynchronized cardioversion due to hypotension (systolic 68, MAP 49)
IV Magnesium Sulfate bolus (first-line for TdP)
STOP Sotalol, Azithromycin, and Ondansetron immediately
Aggressive IV replacement of potassium (K 2.9 mmol/L LOW) and magnesium (1.2 mg/dL LOW)
Consider Isoproterenol infusion if magnesium fails to stabilize rhythm
